source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Evergreen shrub or tree to about 12 m
morphology_documented.leaves: Simple oblong leathery leaves to 20 cm, serrate; dark green above, yellowish-green below, reddish when emerging; petiole 2–3 cm
morphology_documented.flowers: White five-parted flowers 6–8 mm across in 10–16 cm panicles
morphology_documented.habitat: Cultivated, escaping especially on sandy soils

source_scope_note: Species-level and key-level traits distinguished; modern secondary traits stay attributed to their own sources.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Flora documents introduction from East Asia (China, Taiwan, Japan, Sumatra), not native to project target
Retain P. serrulata as historical synonym
preservation: Additive research only, species JSON and photo/attribution/gallery assets unchanged
